pieces.title: How do the pieces move?
pieces.subtitle: Pick a piece to see the squares it can reach.

k.name: King
k.moves: Moves one square in any direction, straight or diagonal. The king may never be left under attack; the whole game is about protecting it.
k.tip: In the endgame the king is a strong piece: bring it to the centre.

q.name: Queen
q.moves: The strongest piece: moves any distance along ranks, files and diagonals. A rook and a bishop in one.
q.tip: Don't bring the queen out too early; your opponent gains time by chasing it.

r.name: Rook
r.moves: Moves any distance along ranks and files, but cannot jump over pieces.
r.tip: Rooks are strongest on open files and on the seventh rank.

b.name: Bishop
b.moves: Moves only diagonally, so it always stays on squares of one colour.
b.tip: Two bishops working together cover the whole board.

n.name: Knight
n.moves: Moves in an L shape: two squares one way, then one to the side. The only piece that can jump over others.
n.tip: A knight is strong in the centre; on the edge it has fewer moves.

p.name: Pawn
p.moves: Moves one square forward, or two from its starting square. It captures one square diagonally forward.
p.tip: A pawn that reaches the last rank turns into any piece, usually a queen.

special.title: Special moves
special.subtitle: Three rules many beginners don't know.

castling.title: Castling
castling.text: The king moves two squares towards a rook, and the rook crosses over to stand beside it. Neither may have moved yet, and the king may not be in check or pass through an attacked square.

enPassant.title: En passant
enPassant.text: When a pawn moves two squares and lands beside an enemy pawn, that pawn may capture it as if it had moved one, but only on the very next move.

promotion.title: Promotion
promotion.text: A pawn that reaches the last rank becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight. Most players pick the queen.

afrasiab.text: Ivory chess pieces found at Afrasiab in Samarkand are among the oldest known in the world.

timur.text: “Tamerlane chess”, linked to the name of Amir Timur, was played on an 11 × 10 board with camels, giraffes and other extra pieces.

shannon.text: Claude Shannon estimated about 10¹²⁰ possible games, far more than there are atoms in the universe.

classics.heading: Classic games
classics.subtitle: The most famous games in chess history — check every move with the engine.

samarkand.title: Victory in Samarkand
samarkand.story: The 2026 Chess Olympiad. In front of a home crowd, Nodirbek Abdusattorov beat Fabiano Caruana: a kingside pawn storm (f4–f5, g4–g5–g6) and the blow 44.Rxg7+ decided the game.

opera.title: The Opera Game
opera.story: Paul Morphy played two noblemen during a performance at the Paris Opera. Fast development, open lines and a queen sacrifice on move 16 — mate with a rook on move 17. The best lesson in opening principles.

immortal.title: The Immortal Game
immortal.story: Adolf Anderssen gave up a bishop, both rooks and his queen, then mated with his remaining minor pieces. The game became the symbol of romantic chess.

evergreen.title: The Evergreen Game
evergreen.story: Anderssen's attacking genius again: after 20.Rxe7+ and the queen sacrifice 21.Qxd7+!! his bishops give mate. Wilhelm Steinitz named it — a game that never fades.

century.title: The Game of the Century
century.story: Thirteen-year-old Bobby Fischer gave up his queen with 17...Be6!! against the strong master Donald Byrne. He took plenty of material in return and mated on move 41.

kasparovTopalov.title: Kasparov's Immortal
kasparovTopalov.story: Kasparov sacrificed a rook with 24.Rxd4!! and chased Black's king across the whole board. Many call it the finest game of his career.

deepBlue.title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
deepBlue.story: The deciding sixth game of the 1997 rematch. After the sacrifice 8.Nxe6, IBM's Deep Blue won in just 19 moves — the first time a computer beat a reigning world champion in a match.

reti.title: An eleven-move miracle
reti.story: Tartakower rushed in the Caro-Kann, and Réti sacrificed his queen with 9.Qd8+!!. Two moves later a bishop gave mate — 11 moves in all.
